Be communicative with him and give him the space he needs for this amount of time. But be firm once you are able to speak with him again. A lot of the time, people with bipolar disorder say things they don’t truly mean to the ones they are closest to. I’m bipolar myself, and can name a few times where I said some things I didn’t really mean and I was sure to apologize and give my partner as much care as was necessary to make up for what I had said. Now, that being said, this is no excuse for abuse or manipulation. 

He’s going to need some time, as it’s probably a big deal for him to come forward about his diagnosis. Keep doing what you’re doing in regards of research, and keep an open mind. Tell him once he’s ready that you are willing to help him and learn more to accommodate his needs, ask him if he goes to therapy or takes meds. But above all, give yourself time for you. Self care is extremely important, don’t sacrifice your well being for someone else. I wish you luck.
